simple.meaning: אֱדַיִן (ʼĕdayin) is a Hebrew object word meaning “then (of time).” BibleIQ follows the concrete thing through the verses where it appears.
simple.biblicalBackground: The occurrence trail begins at Ezra 4:9. The surrounding context includes family line, kingship, prophetic witness.
simple.inThisVerse: In this verse, the tapped English word is source-aligned to אֱדַיִן (H116) in the Hebrew text.
simple.whyItMatters: Concrete words often carry patterns through Scripture because objects, animals, offerings, and created things are used repeatedly in worship, judgment, covenant, and narrative.

Then Daniel returned answer with counsel and prudence to Arioch the captain of the king’s guard, who had gone out to kill the wise men of Babylon.

Then the iron, the clay, the bronze, the silver, and the gold were broken in pieces together, and became like the chaff of the summer threshing floors. The wind carried them away, so that no place was found for them. The stone that struck the image became a great mountain, and filled the whole earth.
Then the king Nebuchadnezzar fell on his face, worshiped Daniel, and commanded that they should offer an offering and sweet odors to him.
Then the king made Daniel great, and gave him many great gifts, and made him rule over the whole province of Babylon, and to be chief governor over all the wise men of Babylon.

definitions.full: H116. edayin אֱדַ֫יִן 57 adverb then, thereupon (so Egyptian Aramaic S-C Pap. H 1, J 1 ), not ᵑ7 : the usually Aramaic forms are הֵידֵין , Mandean האידין (Nö M 207 ); from [ אֱדַי ] = Biblical Hebrew אֲזַי (see אָז ) + determ. affix n (as in תַּמָּן דִּכֵּן, ; in Sabean = post-positive article; Hom Chr. § 57: compare W CG 115 ), Nö GGA 1884, 1020: אֲזַי , [ אֱדַי ], probably from same demonstrative √ as דִּי דָּא, זֶה, , etc., , , lo well then, in that case , Ethiopic : when ? : now (Di Lex. 197, 1072 ), Syriac (enclitic) but ); — then, thereupon , Dan 2:15 , 17 , 19 , 25 , 48 ; 3:24 +, Ezra 4:9 ; 4:23 ; 5:4 ; 5:9 + (always, except 5:5 , at beginning of sentence, introducing new stage of narrative with some emphasis); so with בֵּאדַיִן בְּ, (3 t. Ezra, 26 t. Daniel) Dan 2:14 , 35 , 46 ; 3:3 , 13 , 19 , 21 (twice in verse); 3:26 , etc., Ezra 4:24 ; 5:2 ; 6:1 ; מִןאֱֿדַיִן from that time 5:16 .
